description: A modular-monolith Node.js/Express backend for the Metkart user, vendor, and delivery-boy apps.

services.name: Metkart Backend API
services.description: A single API with modular boundaries for user, vendor, and delivery-boy experiences.

questions.question: Which language should the backend use?
questions.rationale: The request explicitly asks for a Node.js backend.

options.label: Node.js
options.description: JavaScript runtime suited to the requested Express backend.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: A strongly typed option for building APIs on .NET.

options.label: Python
options.description: A concise option for APIs and service development.

options.label: Java
options.description: A strongly typed option commonly used for backend services.

questions.question: Which backend framework should be used?
questions.rationale: The request explicitly specifies Node.js with Express.

options.label: Express
options.description: Minimal, flexible Node.js framework explicitly requested.

options.label: NestJS
options.description: A structured Node.js framework with built-in modular conventions.

options.label: Fastify
options.description: A lightweight Node.js framework focused on performance.

questions.question: What should the backend starter include?
questions.recommendedChoice: A modular monolith with clean folder structure, configurable MongoDB URI, authentication and role-based access for user, vendor, and delivery-boy app access. The user app has food, recycle, mechanic, and grocery categories. Keep domain workflows limited to this scope.
questions.answer: A modular monolith with clean folder structure, configurable MongoDB URI, authentication and role-based access for user, vendor, and delivery-boy app access. The user app has food, recycle, mechanic, and grocery categories. Keep domain workflows limited to this scope.
questions.rationale: This captures the requested structure, app audiences, access model, and MongoDB configuration constraint without inventing broader workflows.

questions.question: Which data stores should the project use?
questions.rationale: The user explicitly requests MongoDB and requires connection configuration to be controlled by the MongoDB URI.

options.label: MongoDB
options.description: Document database requested for the backend.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational database option for structured relational data.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Managed relational database service on Azure.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for files and media.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Choose only when the application does not need persistence, file/object storage, queues, caches, or a service-associated storage account.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in for application API features?
questions.rationale: The request asks for authentication and role-based access control.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users authenticate to access protected application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: The API does not require user sign-in for application features.
